items.title: TRAFFITECH-GH full implementation rescheduled to November 1
items.description: The Ghana Police Service has rescheduled the full implementation of its automated traffic law enforcement programme, TRAFFITECH-GH, from October 1 to November 1, 2026. According to the Police Service, the extension is intended to allow for more extensive public awareness and education on the programme before its full rollout. The education campaign will cover how TRAFFITECH-GH operates, the traffic offences that will be detected and how Electronic Notices of Violation (ENV) will be issued to offending motorists. The programme, being implemented through the Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD), forms part of efforts by the Police Service to address indiscipline on Ghana’s roads and improve compliance with traffic laws and regulations. The Police Service has urged motorists, drivers and vehicle owners to use the additional month to familiarise themselves with the system ahead of the November 1 rollout. In a statement dated September 29, 2026, the Service also expressed appreciation to the media for its support in publicising the programme and said it remains committed to working with stakeholders to ensure the successful implementation of TRAFFITECH-GH to improve road safety.

items.title: À Alger, le patron de l’OPEP contredit le discours sur la fin du pétrole
items.description: L’Organisation des pays exportateurs de pétrole (OPEP) ne partage pas les prévisions de baisse de la consommation de pétrole dans les décennies à venir à cause de la transition énergétique et la montée des énergies renouvelables. Le secrétaire général de l’organisation prévoit même un fort accroissement de la demande mondiale sur l'or noir dont l’Algérie produit un million de barils par jour. En 2050, c'est-à-dire dans 25 ans, la demande mondiale aura augmenté du quart de son niveau actuel. SG de l’OPEP : la demande sur le pétrole va augmenter de 23% d'ici à 2050 Haitham Al Ghais, SG de l’OPEP, est en visite en Algérie, du 26 au 29 septembre. Il a été notamment reçu lundi 28 septembre par le président de la République Abdelmadjid Tebboune. Dans une interview accordée à l’agence officielle APS, El Ghais a livré des estimations sur ce que sera le marché pétrolier d'ici le milieu du siècle. “L'économie mondiale doublera de taille par rapport à aujourd'hui, portée par les économies des pays en développement, ce qui fera grimper la demande de pétrole en 2050 à 124 millions de barils par jour, contre environ 105 millions de barils par jour actuellement”, prévoit-il. Haitham Al Ghais a en outre fait une prévision concernant le gaz naturel, à l’issue de l’audience que lui a accordé le président de la République. Le gaz naturel deviendra la deuxième plus importante source d’énergie à l’horizon 2050, selon les études de l’OPEP et celles de plusieurs autres organismes, a-t-il indiqué. Les prévisions à la baisse, un “message inquiétant” aux investisseurs Pour satisfaire la demande appelée à croître, l’industrie pétrolière mondiale a besoin d’investissements conséquents. Or, le discours actuel sur la transition énergétique et l’abandon des énergies fossiles n'encourage pas les investisseurs. Dans des déclarations à Ennahar, Al Ghais a indiqué que ce qui se dit concernant la baisse de la demande mondiale sur le pétrole envoie un “message inquiétant” aux investisseurs, les incitant à cesser d'injecter de nouveaux capitaux dans ce secteur, ce qui va, selon lui, à l'encontre des appels lancés par l'organisation en faveur de la poursuite des investissements afin de répondre aux besoins énergétiques futurs. L'OPEP estime que l'industrie pétrolière mondiale aura besoin d'investissements cumulés colossaux, s'élevant à 17 700 milliards de dollars d'ici 2050, afin de continuer à répondre à la demande mondiale croissante. L’organisation a toujours considéré que les énergies renouvelables sont “complémentaires” et non une alternative aux énergies fossiles. L’article À Alger, le patron de l'OPEP contredit le discours sur la fin du pétrole est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Burkina Faso : Le Hadj 2027 lancé avec un quota de 8 143 pèlerins et Air Burkina comme transporteur officiel
items.description: Le Hadj 2027 a été officiellement lancé ce 29 septembre 2026. Cette année, 8 143 pèlerins burkinabè pourront prendre part au voyage pour l’accomplissement du 5e pilier de l’islam. Leur transport sera assuré par la compagnie nationale Air Burkina. Pour cette édition, de nouvelles dispositions ont été prises pour assurer le bon déroulement du pèlerinage. Tout d'abord, l'organisation est prise en charge par l'État à travers le Comité national d'organisation du pèlerinage à la Mecque (CNOPM). Il va assurer le recrutement des candidats et le choix des prestataires en Arabie saoudite. Cependant, certaines agences de voyages et de tourisme peuvent se voir attribuer certaines missions de l'Etat. Il y a aussi la mise à jour et la révision des textes encadrant le Hadj, notamment le cahier des charges des agences de voyages/transport et l'arrêté interministériel. Pour ce qui concerne les dispositions techniques et organisationnelles, une nouvelle plateforme numérique a été créée pour faciliter l'inscription des pèlerins. Cela fait suite à des difficultés rencontrées au cours de la précédente édition. « Une fois qu'ils (les pèlerins, NDLR) s'inscrivent, ils choisissent l'agence avec laquelle ils veulent aller, et cette agence à son tour, va veiller à son encadrement. Ce qu'il faut dire comme innovation majeure, est qu'il y a eu des plaintes parce que les gens disent qu'ils n'ont pas eu suffisamment de temps pour s'inscrire. Cette année, on va prendre l'ensemble des pèlerins. Une fois qu'ils sont inscrits, on va procéder à un tirage au sort. Et le quota de 8 143 sera dégagé », a indiqué Amadou Sidibé, président du Comité national d'organisation du pèlerinage à la Mecque. Afin d'assurer aux pèlerins de bonnes conditions de séjour et d’assurer une meilleure coordination pour le suivi du déroulement de l'organisation, il a été institué le regroupement des agences en fonction du nombre de pèlerins. Cela se fait pour optimiser la gestion du séjour, du logement et des transports. Il y a aussi la formation des formateurs en novembre à Djeddah pour mieux former l'ensemble des acteurs de terrain. À cela, s'ajoute le maintien de la prise en compte des repas à Médine et à la Mecque dans le coût global du Hadj et la possibilité de payer le sacrifice directement sur la plateforme saoudienne. Quant au transport, la compagnie nationale Air Burkina assurera de nouveau le transport aérien des pèlerins. « Toutes ces réformes engagées témoignent non seulement des efforts constants de quête par les premières autorités de notre pays d'un bon séjour des pèlerins burkinabè en Terre Sainte, mais aussi d'affirmer notre souveraineté et, pour plus de transparence et d'équité, dans le processus d'organisation du pèlerinage à la Mecque », a indiqué Sibiri de Issa Ouédraogo, conseiller technique du ministre d'État, en charge de l'administration territoriale. A noté que le certificat d'aptitude médicale reste une exigence obligatoire pour tous les candidats au pèlerinage. Un appel à la fermeté a été lancé contre toute tentative de sabotage ou de pratiques contraires aux valeurs islamiques et aux directives nationales. Pour le moment, le coût du Hadj 2027 n'est pas encore connu. Une fois déterminé, le montant sera communiqué à la population, a assuré le comité d'organisation. Cheick Habib Désiré BAYILI Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : Le Hadj 2027 lancé avec un quota de 8 143 pèlerins et Air Burkina comme transporteur officiel est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: ‘Insults must not replace arguments’ – Bagbin cautions political actors against language that could undermine democracy
items.description: Speaker of Parliament Alban Bagbin has urged political actors, particularly Members of Parliament, to exercise greater restraint in their language and conduct, warning that the misuse of free speech could undermine Ghana’s democratic stability. He said Ghana’s democracy, which had been hard-won, could not be sustained by constitutional institutions alone but also required discipline, decency and respect for opposing views. Mr Bagbin made the remarks during Parliament’s emergency sitting on Tuesday, September 29, as the House considered concerns surrounding the abuse of free speech. According to the Speaker, democratic stability should never be taken for granted, stressing that the responsibility for protecting the country’s democratic gains extended beyond Parliament and the courts. “Ghana’s democracy has been hard-won. We should never assume that democratic stability perpetuates itself,” he said. “Not only by constitution, courts, and parliaments, it is also sustained by discipline and decency and a political culture in which citizens can disagree profoundly without ceasing to recognise each other’s humanity and equal citizenship.” Language matters Mr Bagbin placed particular emphasis on the role of language in political discourse, saying words could either help unite the country or deepen existing divisions. He reminded MPs of the influence their words could have on citizens, urging them to be mindful of the consequences of their public statements. “Words can mobilise citizens towards a common national purpose. But words can equally inflame passions and deepen divisions,” he said. The speaker therefore cautioned political actors against allowing their language and conduct to gradually heighten tensions to a point where they become difficult to control. “We must therefore be careful that through the cumulative effect of our language and conduct, we do not push our country towards the precipice from which it becomes increasingly difficult to retreat,” he said. Call for restraint Mr Bagbin said Ghana’s democratic system was too important to be weakened by a political culture in which personal attacks and abuse take the place of substantive debate and persuasion. “Our democracy is too valuable to be endangered by a political culture in which insults replace arguments, abuse replace persuasion, and opponents are treated as enemies. We must pull back from that path,” he stated. He stressed that Parliament had a particular responsibility to demonstrate the kind of political conduct expected in a democratic society. “Members of Parliament must lead that effort. I repeat, members of Parliament must lead that effort,” he said. The Speaker consequently called on the leadership of both sides of the House, as well as other political actors, to moderate their language without compromising their political convictions. “I accordingly call upon members, leadership on both sides of the House, and indeed all political actors to moderate our language and to demonstrate that firmness of conviction need not be accompanied by disrespect,” Mr Bagbin said. Responsibility applies to all Mr Bagbin made it clear that the call for responsible political communication was not directed at one side of the political divide. He said the Majority, minority, and the speaker’s office all had a responsibility to uphold standards of respectful discourse. “This responsibility applies equally to the majority and the minority. It applies to the Chair,” he stated. He further stressed that the expectation of responsible conduct should extend beyond proceedings in the Chamber. “It should apply whether we speak on the floor of the House or at committee, at a press conference, or radio or television, or through social media,” he said.

items.title: Why Did Wallace Shawn Liken Israelis to Nazis?
items.description: T his past weekend, a deplorable minute-long video appeared on my X feed. In it, the instantly recognizable actor and playwright Wallace Shawn, most famous for his role as Vizzini in the classic 1987 film The Princess Bride , delivers a hateful rant belied by his grandfatherly demeanor and dulcet tones. He says, The Israelis invaded somebody else’s territory, they took people’s homes, and they did many of the things that the Nazis did to the Jews. You can’t be more evil than what they’re doing. They are doing evil that is just as great as what the Nazis did. And in some ways, it’s worse, because they kind of boast about it. Hitler had the decency to try to keep it secret. For some reason, Hitler didn’t want people to know he was doing these things to the Jews. It was a secret. The Israelis are almost proud of it and don’t keep it a secret. And it’s demonically evil. Shawn’s analysis of the situation in Israel and Gaza is a moral inversion of the truth. The only party in this conflict to have committed an act of genocidal intent was Hamas. It was Hamas whose members recorded their savage rampage into Israel on October 7, 2023, their house-to-house massacring of Jewish civilians so gruesomely evoking the behavior of the Nazis eight decades earlier. It was Hamas whose insatiable lust for Jewish blood was blocked only by force of arms. And it’s Hamas that boasts about the murder of innocent people—Palestinian and Israeli. The Shawn video, which comes from a 2025 interview with the podcaster Katie Halper, resurfaced at a time when rhetoric accusing Israel of “genocide” is at a peak. Representative Ro Khanna , a likely Democratic presidential candidate; Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont; and the Young Democrats of America are just some of the voices on the left that have accused Israel of “ the crime of crimes .” The sudden prominence of this wholly unfounded allegation, and the casual way in which so many people are hurling it, underscores the degree to which progressives have been radicalized since the 2023 Hamas attack. [ James Loeffler: The hatred that broke American politics ] Shawn is a longtime member of Jewish Voice for Peace, an anti-Zionist organization that attributes “all” of the violence of October 7 and in the preceding decades to “Israeli apartheid and occupation—and United States complicity in that oppression.” A growing number of celebrities, several of them Jewish, have expressed similar ideas. The reemergence of Shawn’s video happened to coincide with the publication of a GQ interview with the actor Adam Brody, who plays a rabbi on the Netflix series Nobody Wants This , the third season of which is coming out next month. Brody, who has been canvassing for Democratic candidates in the run-up to the midterm elections, was asked about Gaza. “Put me down as thinking it’s a genocide,” he answered, as if he were ordering a cheeseburger. (He also said that, although he hadn’t previously spoken publicly about the issue, “I have spoken a lot about it privately.”) The willingness to declare the war in Gaza a genocide has become a litmus test on the left and is likely to play a significant factor in the 2028 Democratic presidential primary. The purpose of the claim is not to establish the facts about an undoubtedly horrific conflict but to increase the stakes in a decades-long effort to delegitimize the Jewish state. Israel’s actions in Gaza lack dolus specialis —the legal term for “specific intent,” which, according to a precedent set by the international tribunal that investigated the Rwandan genocide , means that the perpetrator acted “to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnical, racial, or religious group.” Whatever the extreme rhetoric of some Israeli political leaders, Israel has not attempted to use its abundant military superiority to exterminate the Palestinian people. If it were bent on doing so, it would not have sent ground troops into Gaza and incurred hundreds of fatalities; nor would it have worked with the World Health Organization to vaccinate Palestinian children against polio after an outbreak. Some critics of the Jewish state have been accusing it of genocide since its founding, in 1948; others began making the charge only days into its military response to the Hamas attack—as if nothing the Israelis do short of surrendering their country is permissible. E arly in the interview, Halper refers to Shawn—son of the legendary New Yorker editor William Shawn—as a “recovering liberal,” a term usually used to denote an older conservative looking wistfully on their younger, left-wing past. But Shawn, who accepts the label, places his opposition to Israel in a broader rejection of liberalism—the very tradition that has allowed Jews to achieve so much in America. Until the age of 40, Shawn was a “fairly typical American liberal centrist,” he tells Halper, according to a transcript . “Basically, I believed in the good intentions of Americans, and I believed in the American democratic constitutional system, and I thought many of the Democrats were good people.” Shawn’s views began to change, however, once he realized that “the United States tried to suppress movements for greater liberty in other countries in the world, the goal of that was to benefit the privileged class of my own country, and I was a member of that class. So I actually turned very much against myself and people like me, and I certainly went through a period of extreme nausea and self-hate.” Shawn’s political epiphany occurred during the early years of the Reagan administration, and his views about U.S. iniquity were solidified by his time living in Central America. “I loved being in Nicaragua under the Sandinistas,” Shawn said in a 1991 interview with the Los Angeles Times of the Soviet-backed Marxist-Leninists then running that country. “I personally felt a deep contentment there based on the feeling that maybe things could be done better.” The Sandinistas were peacefully ousted in a democratic election but returned to power in 2007 under the leadership of Daniel Ortega, who canceled this year’s election and has banned the opposition from participating in future ones. If Shawn has criticized Ortega for these genuinely tyrannical actions, there is no public record of it. [ David Frum: Anti-Semitism is becoming mainstream ] Part of what’s so chilling about Halper’s interview with Shawn is that a man of such refined aesthetic tastes and with such a humane demeanor, as exemplified in his critically acclaimed 1981 picture, My Dinner With Andre , could embrace such brutal, uncompromising politics. Exquisitely nuanced in conveying human motivations and emotions in his performances, Shawn is Manichaean and maximalist in his politics. “If you don’t see that it’s evil to do those things to other human beings, then you’re in a different universe from me,” he said of Israeli actions in Gaza, according to the transcript of the Halper interview. “I don’t know how to communicate with you.” There is nothing defensible motivating Israelis; they are driven by an infernal delight in “killing the innocent” and “bombing hospitals.” The notion that Jews might have an equally valid claim to the land, or that the land ought to be divided between the two peoples, is anathema to Shawn. President Woodrow Wilson “was wrong to say that each people should have their own state,” he says. “That hasn’t turned out to be that great, this idea that each ethnic group should have its own state.” And yet, Shawn’s supposed opposition to ethnic-based statehood makes a curious exception for Palestinians, whose right to self-determination he supports. If one accepts the proposition that Israelis are acting like Nazis, there’s no way of avoiding at least a partial justification of October 7. “Even in talking about the horrible attack on October 7 on the Israelis, it’s a little absurd to pretend that that came out of nowhere,” Shawn told Halper. At the same time, he insists that he is “in no position to judge the Palestinians” and is “more of a pacifist as time passes.” Shawn and Halper pride themselves on their expansive empathy, but it’s an empathy that doesn’t extend to Israelis. “I have a lot of hate in my heart,” Halper tells Shawn. “Not to sound corny, but it is based, I think, on the flip side of love. The reason I hate the people I hate is because I love the people that they are killing, oppressing, maiming, torturing.” Shawn’s moral myopia is most fully on display when he blames other Jews, and not anti-Semites, for anti-Semitism. “What Netanyahu has done is unimaginably horrible for Jews, and let’s hope that nobody associates Israelis or Netanyahu with Jews, with you and me,” he tells Halper. “I hope nobody blames me for what they’re doing. But gee.” Few on the left would blame anti-Black racism on the behavior of African governments, and many spoke out forcefully against the spike in anti-Asian hate crimes in the early months of the coronavirus pandemic, which originated in China. But Jews whom they deem to be behaving badly can be held responsible for attacks on other Jews. Shawn was remarkably candid about his motivations in 2009, when he told a British Jewish newspaper, “I find it horrifying that Jews are seen—particularly by a young generation who do not know the history—as victimisers who are very self-righteous about what they do. From a moral point of view it was better when we were victims.” This is the position Jews were in before the creation of Israel: stateless and at the mercy of the powerful. Anti-Semites throughout history have preferred to see Jews cowering before their oppressors. Shawn is entitled to express “self-hate,” but there’s no reason the rest of the world’s Jews should subordinate themselves to this point of view. Whatever moved Shawn to make his remarks last year, they have reappeared at a time when anti-Semitism is flourishing in America like never before. That his comments received so little notice at the time they were spoken shows how routine casual accusations of genocide had already become, and how thoroughly knowledge of history had depreciated. Today, such calumnies are uttered as flippantly as if they were items on a menu, perfectly encapsulating the moral derangement of our times.

items.title: Minority demands full data on Ghana narcotics seizures, arrests and prosecutions since 2025
items.description: The Minority in Parliament has raised concerns about what it describes as weaknesses in Ghana’s security systems, warning that they could expose the country to becoming a major transit point for narcotics. The concerns were raised by the Minority’s spokesperson on Defence and Interior, Rev. John Ntim Fordjour, ahead of Parliament’s emergency sitting on Tuesday, September 29, to discuss recent major narcotics seizures linked to Ghana. The emergency sitting follows the seizure of nearly 3.9 tonnes of cocaine at France’s Port of Dunkirk in a container reportedly shipped from Ghana. Rev. Fordjour said the development raised serious questions about the effectiveness of Ghana’s border controls and the response of state institutions responsible for preventing drug trafficking. He said the Minority was demanding the publication of full, verifiable data on narcotics seizures, arrests and prosecutions recorded in the country since January 2025. “We call on the executive to publish in real time with primary sourcing full and verifiable data on every narcotic seizure, arrest, prosecutions since January 2025, so that we no longer learn the state of our own borders from foreign customs officers,” he said. The Minority spokesperson said the parliamentary inquiry should examine institutional and systemic weaknesses, including the possible involvement or complicity of state agencies, without prejudging cases before the courts. “It will also look into the role and actions of possible complicity of state agencies,” he added. Rev. Fordjour said any committee established by Parliament should have the authority to summon witnesses, compel the production of documents and conduct its proceedings publicly, except where national security considerations require otherwise. He maintained that Parliament had a constitutional responsibility to demand accountability from the Executive rather than leave the matter solely to investigations initiated by government agencies. “Parliament is not a spectator in this matter. The Constitution gives it the power to appoint committees, to summon and to demand answers,” he said. The Minority also called on members of both sides of the House to support efforts to establish the facts, arguing that drug trafficking and substance abuse should not be treated as partisan issues. “The trafficker does not check party cards. The young person destroyed by addiction does not ask which side of the House his member sits on,” Rev. Fordjour said. He urged the government to make the requested information accessible to the public, arguing that transparency would help Ghanaians assess the country’s record in combating narcotics trafficking. “If the government is confident in its record, it has nothing to fear from the truth,” he added.

items.title: Ouahbi : « L’essentiel a été fait, les joueurs ont fait preuve d’une grande discipline »
items.description: L’entraîneur national Mohamed Ouahbi s’est dit satisfait de la prestation de la sélection marocaine face au Lesotho, soulignant que la victoire (2-0) a permis aux Lions de l’Atlas d’atteindre l’objectif fixé et de décrocher trois nouveaux points, portant leur total à six après deux journées des éliminatoires de la Coupe d’Afrique des Nations (CAN) 2027. Lors de la conférence de presse d’après-match, Ouahbi a reconnu que la rencontre n’avait pas été facile, notamment en raison des conditions dans lesquelles elle s’est disputée. Il a notamment relevé que l’état de la pelouse n’avait pas permis au Maroc de développer le football auquel il est habitué, obligeant les joueurs à faire preuve de réalisme et à s’adapter aux circonstances. Le sélectionneur national a souligné que les joueurs marocains avaient affiché « une grande concentration et beaucoup de discipline » tout au long de la rencontre. Il a ajouté qu’un but inscrit rapidement aurait permis à la sélection de mieux contrôler le match, mais que le groupe a finalement réussi à s’imposer tout en préservant sa cage inviolée. Pour Ouahbi, l’importance de cette victoire ne se limite pas aux trois points. Le match a également permis à plusieurs joueurs d’accumuler du temps de jeu, donnant au staff technique davantage d’options et contribuant au développement du groupe dans la perspective des prochaines échéances. Le sélectionneur a estimé que la sélection marocaine évoluait dans une dynamique ascendante, soulignant plusieurs points positifs apparus lors des deux premières rencontres, tout en reconnaissant que certains aspects nécessitaient encore du travail et des ajustements avant les prochains rendez-vous. Concernant la suite des éliminatoires, Ouahbi a indiqué que le Maroc affrontera à deux reprises le Niger avant de retrouver le Gabon. Ces rencontres constitueront de nouvelles étapes pour poursuivre le travail et améliorer la cohésion et le niveau de performance de l’équipe. Le sélectionneur national a enfin insisté sur l’importance de maintenir la concentration et le sérieux, estimant que les six points récoltés en début de parcours constituent une base importante pour la suite des éliminatoires, tout en appelant à poursuivre le travail afin de corriger les insuffisances observées lors des précédentes rencontres. The post Ouahbi : « L’essentiel a été fait, les joueurs ont fait preuve d’une grande discipline » appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Keivo disqualified from Big Brother Naija after physical altercation with Tram
items.description: Big Brother Naija ‘Show Ya Sef’ housemate, Victor Ikpe, popularly known as Keivo, has been disqualified from the reality show after a physical altercation with fellow housemate, Tram. Biggie announced Keivo’s disqualification on Tuesday after showing the housemates clips of the incident, which occurred during the final week of the competition. After reviewing the footage, Big Brother identified Keivo as the perpetrator and ordered his removal from the house. “Keivo, as the perpetrator, has been removed from the house. He is therefore disqualified from the house,” Biggie announced. He also warned the remaining housemates against violence, stressing that such conduct would not be tolerated in the house. “Violence is never an option,” Biggie said. The development followed a confrontation between Keivo and Tram on Monday over a black shirt. Tram had accused Keivo of taking his shirt, but Keivo denied the allegation, insisting that he had a similar shirt. The disagreement escalated after Keivo became upset over being called a thief. The argument later turned physical, with Keivo throwing the first punch before other housemates intervened to separate them. Biggie subsequently instructed the housemates to freeze, while three ninjas entered the house and escorted Keivo out through the storeroom. Before leaving, Keivo became emotional as he explained his side of the incident, saying the disagreement was not really about the shirt but about the accusation that he had taken something belonging to another person. He maintained that he did not want to leave the show with viewers believing he was a thief, saying he was concerned about how the incident could affect his reputation. Keivo’s disqualification came after his name disappeared from the official voting platform earlier on Tuesday, prompting speculation among viewers about his status in the competition. The show wraps up on October 4, with the winner expected to receive a N160m grand prize. The post Keivo disqualified from Big Brother Naija after physical altercation with Tram appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tournée agricole: Cheikh Oumar Bâ à l’écoute des acteurs du riz à Ndiaye
items.description: Le ministre de l’Agriculture, de la Souveraineté alimentaire et de l’Élevage, Dr Cheikh Oumar Bâ, a entamé sa tournée de suivi de la campagne agricole 2026 dans le nord par le département de Dagana. À Ndiaye, il a visité un casier rizicole, le Centre de machinisme agricole et la rizerie de la SFA, avant d’échanger avec les producteurs et les acteurs de la filière riz. DAGANA- Cette première étape de la tournée ministérielle a permis de faire le point sur l’état de la campagne d’hivernage et les difficultés rencontrées par les acteurs de la vallée du fleuve Sénégal. Au casier rizicole de l’Union de Ndiaye, le ministre a échangé avec les producteurs avant de visiter le Centre de machinisme agricole, où la mécanisation a constitué l’un des principaux sujets abordés. La journée s’est achevée à la rizerie de la Société sénégalaise des filières alimentaires (SFA), avec les représentants du Comité interprofessionnel du riz (CIRIZ), de l’Agence nationale de riziculture et des organisations de producteurs et de transformateurs. Le ministre a identifié plusieurs défis, notamment l’aménagement, le drainage, la mécanisation et le coût de l’énergie. « Nous nous apercevons qu’il y a un certain nombre de défis liés à l’aménagement, au besoin de renouveler les aménagements et surtout à la qualité du drainage », a-t-il déclaré. ²Il a également relevé que l’électricité représente environ 40 % du coût de production, faisant de la solarisation une piste de solution. Les échanges ont surtout porté sur les difficultés de commercialisation du riz local. Alioune Diagne, président de l’Association nationale des riziers, a indiqué que 42 000 tonnes étaient en souffrance, dont environ 12 000 tonnes déjà enlevées. « Nous demandons donc que l’État s’assoie avec nous pour essayer de trouver des solutions pérennes », a-t-il plaidé. Le président du CIRIZ, Pape Sandiour Dièye, a également demandé l’accélération de l’enlèvement des stocks afin de faciliter l’écoulement du paddy détenu par les producteurs. De son côté, Mamadou Moustapha Mbodj, président de la Fédération des petites unités de transformation agricole, a sollicité un meilleur accompagnement de l’État, notamment pour l’accès aux subventions et la modernisation des équipements. Pour sa part, Hassane Koffi, directeur général de la SFA, a insisté sur la contractualisation avec les petits producteurs, le financement adapté et la régulation du marché. Il a aussi appelé les Sénégalais à privilégier le riz local. À l’issue des échanges, Dr Cheikh Oumar Bâ a annoncé la poursuite des concertations avec le CIRIZ et l’ANR pour examiner les problèmes et identifier les solutions. « Nous devons être capables, avant même de quitter ici, de voir quels sont les problèmes qu’on peut résoudre sur place », a-t-il indiqué. Jeanne SAGNA (Correspondante)

items.title: Préparatifs de la rentrée scolaire : Mbacké fait face à un déficit d’enseignants et de mobilier
items.description: À quelques jours de la rentrée scolaire, le département de Mbacké fait face à d’importants besoins en personnel enseignant et en mobilier scolaire. L’Inspection de l’éducation et de la formation (IEF) fait état d’un déficit de 53 enseignants pour l’élémentaire et de 23 professeurs pour le moyen secondaire, soit un besoin total de 76 agents. À cela s’ajoute un manque de 12 000 tables-bancs, dont 5 000 pourraient toutefois être réparés. Ces chiffres ont été communiqués par l’Ief de Mbacké, Abdoulaye Oumar Kane, lors de la réunion du Comité départemental de développement de ce mardi 29 septembre 2026 (CDD) consacrée aux préparatifs de la rentrée scolaire. La rencontre, présidée par le sous-préfet de Ndame, Djidiack Kital, s’est tenue en l’absence du préfet de Mbacké et de son adjoint, tous deux empêchés. Selon l’Ief, le déficit en personnel s’explique principalement par les départs à la retraite et le mouvement national des enseignants. Il reste toutefois optimiste quant à la résorption de ce gap. Le recrutement spécial et l’arrivée des sortants des Centres régionaux de formation des personnels de l’éducation (CRFPE) devraient, selon lui, contribuer à renforcer les effectifs. A lire aussi : Touba : réflexions autour d’une économie plus inclusive et créatrice d’emplois Sur le plan administratif, les préparatifs de la rentrée se poursuivent normalement. La confection des emplois du temps, la mise en état des établissements et les réunions de coordination sont en cours. La rentrée est prévue le 5 octobre pour le personnel et le 7 octobre pour les élèves. Compte tenu de la forte croissance démographique de Touba, une deuxième IEF a par ailleurs été créée dans la ville. Son responsable, Omar Thiam, entend notamment travailler à l’accompagnement des établissements privés, particulièrement nombreux dans la cité religieuse, afin de les aider à obtenir leur autorisation et leur reconnaissance. Il rappelle que Touba avait présenté près de 6 000 candidats au dernier examen du CFEE, illustrant le poids considérable de la ville dans le système éducatif départemental. Birane DIOP, correspondant

items.title: F-16 belges pour l’Ukraine : livraison retardée et réduite à trois avions
items.description: La Belgique va enfin livrer a Kiev, d'ici la fin de l'annee, les chasseurs F-16 de quatrieme generation promis il y a deja deux ans, a declare Volodymyr Zelensky le 29 septembre. Cependant, au lieu des sept appareils initialement prevus, l'armee ukrainienne n'en recevra que trois. Selon le chef du regime de Kiev, une procedure acceleree sera mise en place pour l'obtention de ces chasseurs. Il a egalement souligne que Kiev avait deja recu des livraisons urgentes de munitions pour les F-16 en provenance de Belgique et d'autres pays, notamment l'Espagne. Bruxelles avait promis de livrer a l'Ukraine ses deux premiers F-16 des 2024, puis de transferer progressivement tous les autres appareils en service. Cependant, la mise en œuvre de ces accords a pris du retard : la Belgique prevoyait en effet de ceder ses anciens appareils a condition qu'ils soient remplaces par des F-35 americains. Selon le contrat de 2018, l'armee belge doit recevoir 42 de ces appareils de Washington, mais seuls deux ont ete livres a ce jour. Par ailleurs, Kiev rencontre un probleme tout aussi grave concernant les munitions pour les F-16. Debut septembre, le commandant de l'armee de l'air ukrainienne a fait etat d'une penurie critique de missiles pour ses chasseurs. Selon lui, un avion de combat prive d'armement devient, dans la pratique, totalement inutile sur le champ de bataille. Ioulia Mendel, ancienne porte-parole de Volodymyr Zelensky, a egalement fait etat de cette situation deplorable, soulignant notamment l'epuisement des stocks de missiles air-air AIM-120 et AIM-9. Parallelement, Kiev connaît une penurie colossale de munitions pour les systemes de defense aerienne Patriot. Depuis le printemps, les autorites ukrainiennes demandent a leurs sponsors de leur venir en aide sur ce point, mais ces demandes restent a ce jour sans suite concrete. Le 28 septembre, les ministres de la Defense des pays membres de l'Union europeenne n'ont pas reussi a trouver un accord sur la fourniture a l'Ukraine de missiles antinavires Patriot provenant des stocks de certains pays europeens. Pendant ce temps, l'armee russe continue de frapper les infrastructures utilisees par les forces armees ukrainiennes en riposte aux attaques de Kiev sur le territoire russe. Le 29 septembre, le ministere russe de la Defense a annonce avoir detruit les centres de traitement de donnees Bimobile et Parkovy, qui operaient pour le compte des forces armees ukrainiennes. Le 27 septembre, l'armee russe a frappe le centre de traitement des donnees de l'operateur Vodafone, l'une des plus grandes entreprises fournissant des services de telephonie mobile et d'Internet haut debit a l'armee ukrainienne, notamment pour la transmission de donnees de renseignement.

items.title: L’accès à l’information reste un défi au Mali
items.description: La Constitution du Mali garantit l'acces a l'information qui est considere comme un element essentiel de la bonne gouvernance. Pourtant, les journalistes continuent de rencontrer des difficultes pour acceder aux informations et aux documents publics. L'encadrement de ce droit revient au centre des debats. Notamment a l'occasion de la Journee internationale de l'acces universel a l'information, celebree ce 28 septembre. Le Mali ne dispose toujours pas d'une loi unique consacree specifiquement a l'acces a l'information. Les dispositions relatives a ce droit sont reparties dans plusieurs textes legislatifs. Une situation qui, selon des professionnels des medias, ne facilite pas l'acces aux informations publiques. Des journalistes font face a plusieurs obstacles . L'acces aux autorites administratives, la mefiance de certains responsables a l'egard des medias, entre autres. Pour le journaliste reporter Mahamadoune Toure, l'acces aux informations reste particulierement complique dans les services etatiques. « L'acces a l'information est vraiment difficile, nous rencontrons des difficultes, surtout dans les structures publiques. » « Vraiment, on a tous les problemes pour faire reagir les autorites . Malgre la garantie de la Constitution, malgre la presentation de la carte de presse. » De son cote, Yacouba Traore, egalement journaliste reporter, souligne les difficultes rencontrees pour obtenir une reaction des autorites. Ceci, meme lorsque les journalistes disposent de leur carte professionnelle. Les faîtieres de presse demandent le respect du droit Face a ces difficultes, les organisations professionnelles de la presse appellent les services publics et prives a faciliter l'acces aux informations. Daouda Konate, president de l'Union nationale des journalistes du Mali, rappelle que ce droit est garanti par l'article 15 de la Constitution du 22 juillet 2023. Selon lui, la retention d'informations et les lourdeurs administratives restent des obstacles majeurs pour les professionnels des medias et les citoyens. Daouda Konate rappelle egalement que la question de l'acces a l'information avait deja ete prise en compte dans les textes elabores dans le cadre de la refondation de la presse en 2021. « C'est un droit aujourd'hui, c'est un droit pour les journalistes, c'est un droit pour les citoyens », ajoute le responsable de l'UNJM. En l'absence d'un texte unifie et operationnel, les journalistes continuent ainsi d'exercer leur mission d'information. Ils doivent composer avec des difficultes liees notamment aux procedures administratives, a l'acces aux documents officiels et, dans certains cas, au secret administratif. items.title: Burkina: 136 nouveaux officiers spécialistes prêts à relever le défi de la défense de la Patrie
items.description: L’Académie militaire Georges Namoano a consacré, ce mardi 29 septembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, la sortie de 136 officiers spécialistes, désormais appelés à mettre leurs compétences au service des Forces armées nationales et de la Nation. Ils sont ingénieurs en génie civil, informaticiens, psychologues, médecins et spécialistes de plusieurs autres domaines. Au total, 136 élèves officiers spécialistes (EOS) ont reçu leurs épaulettes, à l’occasion de la cérémonie officielle organisée par l’Académie militaire Georges Namoano. Parmi eux figurent 103 EOS de la 16e promotion et 33 EOS issus du continuum. Répartis dans 29 spécialités, ces nouveaux officiers franchissent ainsi une étape majeure de leur parcours militaire, avec pour mission de mettre leur expertise au service de l’armée et du Burkina Faso. Mohamed Salif Lionel Zorom, EOS de la 16e promotion de l'Académie militaire Georges Namoano, entouré de ses proches. Parmi ces 136 officiers spécialistes figure notamment Mohamed Salif Lionel Zorom, médecin, dont le parcours académique illustre la diversité des profils désormais mobilisés au sein des Forces armées nationales. Il avait soutenu, le jeudi 26 juin 2025, sa thèse de doctorat d’État en médecine, avant de franchir aujourd’hui une nouvelle étape avec le port de ses épaulettes. Durant 11 mois, ils ont alterné enseignements théoriques et pratiques, avec une formation académique et militaire axée notamment sur les connaissances scientifiques de niveau chef de groupe, avec une ouverture sur le niveau technique. Leur cursus a également intégré des modules spécifiques consacrés à la connaissance des armes et des services, ainsi qu’un stage pratique de trois semaines au combat au sein de différents corps de troupes. Le délégué de la promotion, Dramane Ouattara Prenant la parole au nom de ses camarades, le délégué de la promotion, Dramane Ouattara, a salué l’engagement des encadreurs et assuré de la détermination des nouveaux officiers à servir la Nation. «Nous exprimons notre profonde gratitude à nos encadreurs pour les efforts consentis tout au long de notre formation. Forts des connaissances et des compétences acquises, nous sommes désormais prêts à les mettre au profit de la Nation et à répondre, avec engagement et responsabilité, aux missions qui nous seront confiées», a déclaré le délégué Ouattara. Le ministre d'État, ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, Célestin Simporé Patron de la cérémonie, le ministre d’État, ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, Célestin Simporé, a d’abord rendu hommage aux encadreurs pour leur contribution à la formation de ces nouveaux officiers. «Je félicite l’ensemble des encadreurs pour les efforts consentis et leur engagement dans la formation de ces officiers spécialistes. Leur travail contribue à renforcer les capacités et le professionnalisme de notre armée», a dit le ministre en charge de la Guerre. Le ministre a également félicité les nouveaux impétrants, tout en les appelant à inscrire leur engagement dans la dynamique actuelle de défense de la patrie. «Dans le contexte de lutte contre le terrorisme que connaît notre pays, je les invite à rester pleinement engagés, disciplinés et déterminés à mettre leurs compétences au service de la défense de la patrie», a poursuivi le ministre Simporé. Cérémonie officielle de la sortie de 136 officiers spécialistes de l'Académie militaire Georges Namoano Pour le ministre d’État, cette sortie de promotion traduit, par ailleurs, la volonté du chef de l’État, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, de renforcer une armée professionnelle, conformément à sa vision de bâtir «une armée professionnelle à la hauteur des attentes de tous les Burkinabè». Photo de famille Avec ces 136 nouveaux officiers spécialistes, l’armée burkinabè étoffe ainsi ses compétences dans des domaines aussi variés que le génie civil, l’informatique, la psychologie ou encore la médecine, au moment où le pays poursuit ses efforts dans la lutte contre le terrorisme. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Burkina: 136 nouveaux officiers spécialistes prêts à relever le défi de la défense de la Patrie est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Tinubu transmits bills on medical college, research fund
items.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has transmitted two bills to the House of Representatives seeking to amend the law governing the National Postgraduate Medical College and establish a National Research Development Fund. The two bills were contained in separate letters dated August 24, 2026, addressed to the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, and received by the House on September 24, 2026. In the first letter, titled “Transmission of National Postgraduate Medical College (Amendment) Bill, 2026 for Passage into Law,” Tinubu asked the House to consider amendments to the law governing the institution. According to the President, the Bill seeks, among other provisions, to reflect the change in the institution’s name and expand its mandate to include the award of Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D) degrees in Clinical Medicine, Dentistry and related fields. He said the Federal Ministry of Justice had vetted and finalised the Bill in line with drafting standards and constitutional provisions. Tinubu urged the House to consider and pass the proposed legislation into law. In the second letter, titled “Transmission of National Research Development Fund (Establishment) Bill, 2026 for Passage into Law,” the President said the proposed legislation was aimed at consolidating research financing and ensuring more efficient utilisation of available resources. He explained that the Bill seeks to bring fragmented research and development funds across Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) under a central National Research Development Fund, through which research agencies and academic institutions could access funding. According to him, the proposed fund would operate as a competitive central funding mechanism to promote collaboration among research agencies, academic institutions and the private sector. Tinubu said the initiative would also support innovation, improve the allocation of research resources in line with national priorities, promote transparency in funding decisions and facilitate the commercialisation of locally developed technologies. The President proposed that the National Research Development Fund be established as an agency under the supervision of the Federal Ministry of Innovation, Science and Technology, with direct funding from the Nigeria Content Development Fund (NCDF). He said the proposed legislation was necessary against the backdrop of the proliferation of research institutes and agencies operating in Nigeria’s research, development and commercialisation space, with each currently operating under separate mandates and budgetary allocations. Tinubu said the proposed central funding mechanism would enable more effective management of the limited financial resources available to research institutes and agencies. He added that the Bill had been reviewed by relevant stakeholders, including the Ministries of Education, Innovation, Science and Technology, and Justice, to ensure alignment with national education objectives, scientific innovation priorities and existing legal and institutional frameworks. Both bills were subsequently forwarded to the House of Representatives for legislative consideration and action. items.title: Coopération Togo-Russie : les experts préparent de nouveaux engagements bilatéraux
items.description: Lomé, 29 sept. (ATOP) – Les experts togolais et russes ont entamé, le mardi 29 septembre à Lomé, les travaux de la première session de la Commission intergouvernementale de suivi des accords de partenariat entre les deux pays. Les échanges portent sur la structuration des axes de coopération et la préparation de nouveaux engagements, à savoir un protocole et trois documents conjoints dans les domaines de la science et de l’éducation. La délégation russe Les travaux sont co-présidés par Mme Angelina Zuikova, chef du département des pays africains, au ministère du développement économique de la Fédération de Russie et M. Ahodo-Abalo Tchamdja, directeur des études et des analyses économiques au ministère en charge de la Veille stratégique du Togo. Ils s’inscrivent dans la dynamique de redynamisation des relations bilatérales entre les deux pays, établies depuis 1960. La session vise à élargir les domaines de coopération et à traduire les orientations des deux gouvernements en actions concrètes. Les experts examineront, au sein des sous-commissions et groupes de travail, plusieurs dossiers d’intérêt commun portant notamment sur le numérique, les mines, la technologie, le commerce, l’économie, les sciences, les transports, l’éducation et l’économie bleue. Les experts togolais et russes sont appelés à traduire les orientations de leurs gouvernements en projets concrets et en mémorandums d’entente, afin de jeter des bases solides à de nouveaux accords de coopération entre les deux pays. « Notre responsabilité commune durant ces travaux est d’évaluer et de structurer les axes stratégiques de notre partenariat bilatéral que nous voulons très dynamiques, pragmatiques et mutuellement bénéfiques », a déclaré M. Tchamdja. Il a fait savoir que, le rôle des experts est à la fois technique et stratégique. Il consiste notamment à formuler des propositions et des solutions réalistes susceptibles d’éclairer la prise de décision et d’être soumises à la validation des ministres des deux pays lors de la session ministérielle. M. Tengue échangeant avec la délégation russe sur les potentialités du Port autonome de Lomé Pour Mme Zuikova, la mise en place d’un mécanisme structuré de dialogue intergouvernemental devrait donner une nouvelle impulsion aux relations entre le Togo et la Russie et permettre de les inscrire dans un cadre durable. « Le Togo est pour nous un partenaire important sur le continent africain, tant dans le domaine commercial et économique que dans le domaine culturel et humanitaire », a-t-elle souligné. Elle a annoncé qu’en plus du protocole de la session, trois documents conjoints supplémentaires, dans les domaines de la science et de l’éducation, seront signés. Ces engagements, selon elle, traduisent la volonté des deux parties d’étendre leur coopération à un large éventail de secteurs. Dans le cadre de cette dynamique, les experts russes ont également visité le Port de Lomé et la Plateforme industrielle d’Adétikopé (PIA) afin de mieux apprécier les potentialités économiques et les opportunités d’investissement offertes par le Togo. Les conclusions des travaux des experts seront soumises à la conférence des ministres, prévue le jeudi 1 er octobre, pour examen et signature. ATOP/HKM/AO

items.title: El novio de Ana Buza niega que la matara atropellándola con el coche y asegura que trató de agarrarla cuando ella se tiró
items.description: “Escucho una bocanada de aire, me giro y la veo cayendo y trato de agarrarla, me incorporo, se desvía el coche y no puedo explicar por qué acaba allí”. Es la explicación que ha dado Rafael V., de cómo murió su entonces novia, Ana Buza, la joven sevillana de 19 años que fue encontrada muerta detrás de un quitamiedos en el kilómetro 511 de la A-4, en la salida dirección a Carmona, el 7 de septiembre de 2019. Después de sesiones maratonianas en las que peritos y forenses han tratado de demostrar si la chica se quitó la vida saltando del vehículo que circulaba a 117 kilómetros por hora —cuando debía hacerlo a 80—, o si fue atropellada por su expareja, como esgrimen, respectivamente, la defensa y la acusación particular, ha llegado el turno del acusado. Rafael ha respondido únicamente a las preguntas de la Fiscalía, que pide tres años de prisión por homicidio imprudente, y a las de su letrado, que solicita la absolución, y se ha acogido a su derecho a no responder al cuestionario de la acusación particular, que reclama 20 años de cárcel por homicidio doloso, por “no querer colaborar en imponer su mentira”. “Llevo siete años de barbaridades”, ha incidido. items.title: Média : Des services de la TVT et de Radio Lomé désormais accessibles en ligne
items.description: Lomé, 29 sept. (ATOP) – Dix services de la Télévision Togolaise (TVT) et de Radio Lomé sont désormais accessibles en ligne, à compter du lundi 28 septembre, a annoncé le ministère de la Communication. « Cette avancée s’inscrit dans le cadre du Programme d’accélération de la digitalisation des services publics (PAD), mis en œuvre par le ministère de l’Efficacité du service public et de la Transformation numérique », a indiqué le communiqué du ministère. L’objectif de cette démarche est de « simplifier l’accès aux prestations, réduire les démarches physiques et améliorer la célérité du traitement des demandes ». Pour le compte de la TVT, les services concernés sont, entre autres, la demande de diffusion de communiqués et avis divers, de retransmission en direct, de diffusion d’un publireportage, de diffusion de bandes défilantes et la demande de diffusion de spot publicitaire ou de sensibilisation. Sur Radio Lomé, on retrouve, la demande de retransmission en direct, de diffusion de bandes défilantes, de couverture médiatique, de diffusion de spot publicitaire ou de sensibilisation et la demande de diffusion d’un avis de décès La mise en ligne de ces dix prestations, précise le communiqué, constitue une première étape dans la transformation numérique des médias publics et contribue à l’amélioration continue de la qualité de service. Les différents services sont disponibles sur la plateforme : www.new.service-public.gouv.tg . ATOP/AJA/BA

items.title: Man City found guilty of all charges of financial rule breaches, Premier League confirms
items.description: Manchester City have been found guilty of all charges of serious breaches of the Premier ​League’s financial rules between the 2009/10 and 2017/18 seasons, the ‌league said in a statement on Tuesday. City were charged in February 2023 with breaches of the league’s financial rules spanning nine seasons following a ​four-year investigation. The Misinformation Monitor newsletter rounds up international misinformation narratives and includes a “Real or Fake?” quiz in every edition. Sign up here. The club said in a statement it would appeal “on ​the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, ⁠of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe”. An independent commission found ​that City “arranged ‘sham’ contracts (which misrepresented the true agreement between the parties) with ​a number of its commercial partners,” the league said. The league added that the commission had found City used schemes “to artificially inflate the club’s revenues, and reduce ​its costs, by more than £900 million during the affected period, ​to appear to comply with financial rules.” “The core decision… details how the club ‌systematically ⁠broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade,” said Richard Masters, the chief executive of the Premier League. “There are elements of the case that remain to be decided, including, importantly, what sanction must ​follow for these breaches.” City, ​who deny ⁠any wrongdoing, said they were disappointed and surprised by the commission’s opinion. “The Club is innocent of the ​accusations made by the Premier League and a ​comprehensive body ⁠of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case,” the club said. “Manchester City FC will now ⁠pursue the ​appeal avenues open to it, on ​the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and ​is unsafe.”

items.title: Gaza’s Open Horizon
items.description: Here in Gaza, war has changed everything, even the sea. During the long, hot summer, children went to the beach either early in the morning or just before sunset. They stepped around piles of garbage, and the tents of displaced families, to wade into water contaminated by sewage. And yet, they went. We all did. And I think we always will. I recently started aiming to take 10,000 steps a day, to get back in shape. To reach that number, I walk from my home to the seafront road and back. I have been doing this for a month now. The distance to the shore and back happens to be 10,000 steps. Which means that, really, my aim was never the step count, but the Mediterranean. I go before sunset, when the heat starts to ease slightly. Not that it ever gets truly cool. July and August brought the worst of the humidity, which sometimes reached 86 percent. As I walk, I watch the sunlight stretch across the water before it slowly disappears. A few children still fly kites along the beach. Kite-flying was common in Gaza before the war and even during it—just a month ago, the sky above the sea was full of kites almost constantly—but now it has become an act of defiance, because the Israelis have said that they will treat kite-flying as a hostile act, on the grounds that kites were sometimes used , before the war, to launch incendiary devices into Israel. In the past, children fashioned kites from brightly colored paper and wooden sticks they bought at stationery stores. Now they improvise, using whatever they can find. Some work with dry palm fronds. I met a boy who had carved his kite’s frame from a long piece of wood; others weave frames from plastic bags, or from the sacks that once carried flour and food aid, joining the edges with torn scraps from old notebooks. [ Ghada Abdulfattah: Feeding a family of seven in Gaza ] Everyone in Gaza is a sea person. That 25-mile coastline is more than a place to walk or fly a kite; it’s a point of access to the outside world. In past summers, all of Gaza would seem to be at the shore—sitting on the beach, or maybe higher up, in wooden chairs near the road. Children dashed in and out of the water, or rode camels or horses along the water for a small fee. Vendors sold grilled corn, lupin beans, and cotton candy, circulating among the blankets with sweet tea and roasted seeds. Some families pitched tents right at the shoreline. People posed there for selfies or wedding photos. The air smelled of corn and charcoal; you’d hear the clatter of backgammon stones, the hiss of a narghile being lit. Sometimes the sound of the sea drowned out nearly everything else. One of my enduring memories of the seashore is from July 2023. My nephews and nieces dug holes in the sand to bury themselves, then ran to the water to wash off, then came back to start digging all over again. The adults swam, pretended to swim, pushed whoever wasn’t swimming into the water anyway. We cracked open a watermelon, hoping it would be ripe—too sweet, too red, and a little sandy, the way we liked it. When I was about 6 years old, my parents took us to the beach to crack open a watermelon just like that. My siblings and I still laugh about this when we remember: Did we go to the sea just to eat a watermelon and go home? No swimming, no playing, no walking—just the watermelon, and then back. Now the stretch of sand where we did this has become a makeshift camp crowded with families displaced from the north and south of the Gaza Strip. We are more than 2 million people living on a ribbon of land about 25 miles long and seven and a half miles wide. This makes Gaza one of the most densely populated places on earth. Before the war, to leave the Strip from any direction required a permit. But the sea asked for nothing. You didn’t need a document to look at it, to wade into it, to let your eyes follow it to a horizon with no drone or checkpoint in sight. The sea was our open horizon, the place we went when we needed to breathe. When I was in a bad mood, my mother would tell me to go there. In the last years before the war, the shore was lined with tourist facilities: chalets, amusement parks, restaurants, and other amenities that welcomed thousands of visitors every summer. Now these are mostly gone, and the few that remain are affordable for only a privileged few. Throughout the Strip, prices are high, air strikes continue, and about half of Gazans now live in tents, which offer little shelter from the scorching summer heat. More than 60 percent of Gaza has become inaccessible, as the so-called yellow line expands westward, pushing people ever closer to the sea. For many of us, the need to be in contact with the water has grown as the space around us has constricted: A person needs a place—any place—to escape the feeling of being trapped. A few weeks ago, I met a fisherman named Hasan Shehada. He told me that Gaza’s port services and many of its fishing boats had been destroyed in the war, and that going out on the water is still dangerous because of Israeli naval fire. Before the war, together with other fishermen, some of them his siblings and cousins, he could bring in enough fish to feed his eight-member family and still earn an income. Now he lacks the boats or equipment that once made this work possible. [ Ahmed Fouad Alkhatib: Flying over my battered homeland ] “The war has changed our sea too,” he told me. “Sometimes I sit on the beach and cry, thinking about where we were and where we are now.” Now the season is turning. For the families living in tents along the shore, the sea is no longer a place of rest: The sand is windblown and gets into everything, the air is heavy with humidity, and the tents will protect their occupants from the coming cold as little as they did them from the heat that has only just subsided. Still they are patched together against whatever the day might bring. Perhaps looking out at the water will make this bearable—will allow me not to see the tents, if only for a moment, by fixing my eyes on something wider. Sometimes I ask myself: What if Gaza had no sea? What if it were landlocked? I cannot let myself contemplate the answer.

items.title: Iyabo Obasanjo raises alarm over campaign attack
items.description: Says 2027 polls must not be compromised By Adesina Wahab Senator Iyabo Obasanjo has raised the alarm over what she described as renewed threats to her life following an attack on a campaign gathering of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Abeokuta, Ogun State, on Monday. Obasanjo, the PDP candidate for Ogun Central Senatorial District in the forthcoming National Assembly election, said she was putting the United Nations, the United States Embassy in Nigeria and the international community on notice over what she described as threats to her life and the integrity of the January 2027 elections. The former senator spoke in an interview with Splash FM late Monday while reacting to the disruption of a PDP campaign gathering at Ward 16, Trailer Park, Soyooye area of Abeokuta North Local Government Area. According to her, she had seen videos circulating online showing men, some of them masked and allegedly armed with cutlasses, dismantling campaign canopies and attacking people at the venue shortly before her arrival. She warned that unless what she described as growing political violence was stopped, she and her political associates would seek the attention of the international community. “This is not the first time they are making attempts at my life,” she alleged, recalling an incident during the 2003 election in which she said gunmen fired at a vehicle in her convoy, believing she was travelling in it. She claimed that the attack resulted in the death of all the occupants of the vehicle. “I say it aloud now. If anything happens to me, the whole world should know those who are behind it,” she declared. The senator’s comments followed Monday’s disruption of the PDP campaign gathering in the Soyooye area, where witnesses said a group of armed men invaded the venue shortly before the arrival of PDP governorship candidate, Hon. Ladi Adebutu, and Obasanjo. The men, reportedly numbering more than 10, were said to have been armed with cutlasses, axes and other dangerous weapons. The incident reportedly forced the campaign team to temporarily hold back from the venue as tension mounted. Adebutu and Obasanjo later arrived at the campaign ground and met supporters who had gathered for the event, as well as evidence of the earlier disturbance, including damaged chairs and tables. Some people were also said to have sustained injuries. The politicians subsequently contacted security authorities, including the Ogun State Police Command and the Department of State Services (DSS), following which a detachment of police and DSS operatives arrived at the scene. Initial accounts circulating online alleged that some supporters were attacked and robbed of their mobile phones and other valuables, while campaign materials were also reportedly damaged. However, the identity and political affiliation of the alleged attackers had not been independently established as of the time of filing this report. The Police Public Relations Officer in Ogun State, Seyi Babaseyi, when contacted on Monday, could not immediately confirm the circumstances surrounding the incident and requested that inquiries be sent to him by text message. No response had been received as of press time. In her subsequent Splash FM interview, Obasanjo linked the incident to what she described as a broader pattern of threats against her. She also questioned what she described as continuing interest by her former political associates in the circumstances surrounding her departure from the All Progressives Congress (APC) and subsequent membership of the PDP. “They showed clearly they do not want me in APC. They treated me like scum and I left their party for them and got into a party that openly embraced me,” she said. “So, why are they still concerned about me when I resigned from their party and the internal affairs details of my own party, PDP?” Obasanjo’s remarks have added a new dimension to Monday’s incident, coming amid preparations for the January 2027 National Assembly election in Ogun State. She called for heightened attention to the safety of political actors and supporters, warning that continued violence could undermine confidence in the electoral process. Her allegations concerning the identity and motives of those behind the incident remain claims requiring investigation and independent verification. items.title: Italian court sentences 3 Egyptian officers to jail in Regeni murder case
items.description: An Italian court sentenced on Monday three Egyptian security officers to 10 years imprisonment in absentia for the 2016 kidnapping of Giulio Regeni. The convicted officers are Major Magdy Sherif of the National Security Agency and police officers Colonel Ather Kamal and Colonel Hesham Helmy. The court dismissed the charge of conspiracy to commit aggravated murder that was leveled against Sherif, while another security official implicated in the case, Major General Tarek Saber, was acquitted of all charges. The Italian prosecution had requested in its closing arguments a life sentence for Sherif and 17 years and six months for the three other defendants. “A ruling issued in the name of the Italian people, a ruling that stands as a safeguard for all the Giulios and Giulias of the world,” said Alessandra Ballerini, the family’s lawyer. Ballerini added that the verdict proves that the body of evidence presented before the court withstood its scrutiny. “From this evening on, all regimes, along with their apparatuses and agents, will be forced to remember that human dignity is inviolable, as are human bodies; that impunity can be defeated; and that democracies can put a stop to arbitrary abuse,” she added. Riccardo Noury, Amnesty International Italy’s spokesperson, believes the verdict played an important role in “scratching the wall of impunity built by the Egyptian authorities, since it found three security service officials guilty of a serious crime of international law. It is a victory for human rights and for accountability.” But Noury added that a full read out of the verdict needs to take place. “There was not sufficient evidence to corroborate the charge of murder. As for the crime of torture, no one of the accused was found guilty, because in 2016 torture was not recognized as a crime in the Italian law. Otherwise, the sentences could have been harder.” Yet, “the Italian judiciary was our best ally,” Noury concluded, adding that the Italian authorities might not welcome the verdict. In his statements following the verdict, Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said that “Egypt has not been convicted, three people have been convicted,” in a nod to how the verdict would not affect bilateral relations. Tajani was in Cairo earlier in September to sign off some bilateral agreements concerning human trafficking and irregular migration. Meanwhile, Italian Prime Minister Georgia Meloni made a major visit to Egypt in March 2024 , alongside other European leaders, to sign off the “comprehensive strategic agreement” between Egypt and the European Union, which elevated relations, including with a 7.4 billion euro in financial support. On the Egyptian front, a government source told Mada Masr that a high-level call between the Egyptian and Italian leaderships took place ahead of the verdict to find a legal way out that takes into consideration the nature of bilateral relations. According to Italian law, there are levels of appeal before a final ruling is reached, and it is not believed at this time that there will be any requests for the accused’s extradition to Italy. *** A PhD student at the University of Cambridge, 28-year old Regeni had been in Egypt studying independent trade unions when he disappeared from a downtown Cairo metro station while on his way to meet a friend on January 25, 2016, the fifth anniversary of the 2011 revolution. His body was found just over a week later on February 3 by a highway on the outskirts of Cairo. Upon hearing that a body had been discovered, then-Italian ambassador to Egypt Maurizio Massari promptly visited Zeinhom morgue. He and his entourage were at first refused entry but after their insisting were allowed in, where they found Regeni’s body disfigured, showing marks of heavy torture. A joint Italian-Egyptian investigation was launched. Egyptian investigators initially denied that Regeni’s body bore marks of torture and gave a number of narratives behind his murder, including that he died in a car accident, before announcing in March 2016 that they had killed five members of a criminal gang specialized in robbing foreigners and impersonating police officers, as well as the discovery of Regeni’s passport and personal belongings in a flat owned by one of the gang members’ sister. Italian investigators rejected this account, with information subsequently showing that the gang’s alleged leader was more than 100 km away from Cairo at the time of Regeni’s disappearance. In April 2016, Rome recalled its ambassador, Maurizio Massari, owing to its view that Egypt had not sufficiently cooperated in helping uncover the truth of the crime. Shortly after, the European Parliament condemned the killing of Regeni and recommended that EU countries halt the export of military equipment to Egypt. In June, the Italian parliament blocked the export of parts of F-16 fighter jets as part of an effort to pressure Egyptian authorities to increase cooperation in the investigation. In the same month, Reuters reported that plain clothes policemen had arrested Regeni near the Gamal Abdel Nasser metro station on the evening of January 25 and detained him at a security headquarters. At this point, the official Egyptian account shifted from complete denial, when the Egyptian public prosecutor acknowledged in September that police had been surveilling Regeni before his disappearance and that the independent street vendors union head, Mohamed Abdallah, filed a report about him on January 7. The acknowledgment came after months of denying that Regeni had been under any security surveillance. Then, in January 2017, Egyptian television aired part of a video Abdallah had secretly filmed of Regeni, showing the union head asking him for money for personal use, a request which was refused. The Egyptian prosecution said that the recording was among the materials submitted to Italian investigators and that security authorities had stopped monitoring Regeni after concluding that his activities did not affect national security. But an Italian diplomatic source told Mada Masr at the time that the clip was cut from a longer video which also showed connections between Abdallah and the entities that put him up to the recording. With the continuation of the investigation, the case gradually shifted from a search for an unknown killer toward the identification of individuals within Egypt’s security apparatus. In April 2017, an Italian source familiar with the investigation revealed to Mada Masr that investigators initially prepared a list of 26 names, but after Egyptian officials whose implication only went as far as having knowledge of the crime were discounted, there remained on the list 10 people believed by investigators to be connected to the acts of kidnapping, torture and body disposal. Despite the case remaining unresolved, the diplomatic crisis began to subside . In August 2017, in a move triggering strong domestic criticism, Italy reinstated its ambassador to Egypt after 16 months of absence. Meanwhile, cooperation between the two countries on energy, migration, Libya and trade was able to resume. And, by 2018, an Egyptian source told Mada Masr that Italy was seeking to redress the economic and political losses it had suffered during the period of tension, while the Italian investigation was ongoing. In February 2020, Mada Masr reported on Cairo’s move to purchase two frigates from the Italian company, Fincantieri, amid increased bilateral cooperation. In May of the same year, a larger arms deal with a total value ranging between 9 and 10 billion euros was delayed due to objections from the Italian government bemoaning the stalling of the investigation. The delayed deal included six frigates, 24 fighter jets, 24 training aircraft and a satellite. The Italian government nonetheless greenlit in June 2020 the sale of two FREMM frigates worth nearly 1.2 billion euros, as part of the larger deal, all despite political and parliamentary objections pointing to the lack of progress in the Regeni case. At the time, Regeni’s family said they felt “betrayed” by the decision to sell the two naval vessels. Alongside the arms industry, the energy sector also featured as one the most prominent areas that saw economic cooperation expand amid the Regeni crisis. In April 2016, weeks after Regeni’s body was found, the Petroleum Ministry announced that Italian energy giant Eni had begun drilling a fourth well in the Zohr gas field as part of a planned investment package of around US$12 billion. Alongside this, Italian company Edison was also advancing in the development of the second phase of the Abu Gir gas field, with investments estimated at around $220 million. By February 2020, economic relations between the two countries had strengthened . Eni’s total investments in Egypt exceeded $13 billion, according to the corporation’s president, while the development of new wells in Zohr and the expansion in oil and gas concessions in the Western Desert were in full swing, all in parallel to the ever widening commercial and industrial cooperation between the two countries. The investigation took a more specific form in 2018 when the prosecution in Rome officially added five Egyptian officers to the list of suspects, with Ballerini announcing their names: Tarek Saber, Magdy Sherif, Hesham Helmy, Asser Kamal and Mahmoud Negm. She added that the family’s legal team came up with a broader list of 20 names, most of whom were officials in the Interior Ministry’s state security sector. And on December 10, 2020, while the trade negotiations and arms deals were ongoing, the Italian prosecution officially charged four of those five, namely Tarek Saber, Hesham Helmy, Asser Kamal and Magdy Sherif, and it dropped the charges against Negm due to insufficient evidence. At the time, Mada Masr quoted an Egyptian government source describing the two countries as having reached an understanding whereby each party could follow its own course on the issue, while also allowing friendly relations to continue between Cairo and Rome. This led to the Egyptian prosecution officially ending its investigation in December 2020 with the announcement of there being “no grounds to file a criminal case due to the unknown identity of the perpetrator.” The prosecution also rejected the Italian findings regarding the Egyptian officers. In May 2021, considering there to be sufficient evidence to continue the case, an Italian judge ordered that the four officers be tried in absentia and set the trial’s start date to October. On the scheduled date, the court suspended the trial due to the Italian authorities’ inability to formally notify the defendants of their indictment, which is required by Italian law, after failing to obtain their official residency addresses from Egyptian authorities. The trial thus remained held up until the end of 2023, when Italy’s supreme court ruled that a foreign country’s lack of cooperation in helping locate the accused should not pose an obstruction to the trial. Noury explained to Mada Masr that the court’s decision was based on the defendant’s knowledge of the accusations levied against them and that the Italian judiciary had repeatedly requested from Egyptian authorities that they provide the defendants’ addresses. In February 2024, the Rome court resumed the trial of the four officers in absentia. The Italian prosecution said that Egyptian investigators did not respond to 39 of 64 requests for information and that some of the materials received by Italy did not benefit the investigation. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, as well as former Italian prime ministers and ministers, were also named in a list of those requested to be heard as witnesses. During the closing arguments last June, the prosecution requested a life sentence for Magdy Sherif, and 17 years and six months in prison for the other three defendants. The session featured, for the first time, the presentation of autopsy images of Regeni’s body with his family’s consent, and the prosecution stated that they supported the accusation that the researcher was subjected to systematic torture over several days. The post Italian court sentences 3 Egyptian officers to jail in Regeni murder case first appeared on Mada Masr .
